Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: 3 days of severe diarrhea and persistent vomiting; described as initially watery then very loose stools; vomiting everything including liquids.
- Onset/duration/progression: Symptoms began 3 days ago and have not improved; vomiting most recently after breakfast this morning (~2 hours prior to consult).
- Associated symptoms: Subjective high temperature ("feeling literally roasting"); intermittent periumbilical abdominal pain centered around the navel with strong urge to defecate when pain occurs; passing urine (last passed ~1 hour ago); no blood in stool or urine.
- Exposures: Close contact with brother who has similar symptoms; patient reports possible school-wide illness per brother.
- Bowel habit baseline: Normally one bowel movement each morning; no prior history of diarrhea or constipation.
- Past medical history / surgeries: No significant medical history reported other than routine menstrual cramps; no prior abdominal surgeries reported.
- Medications:
  - Vitamin D — taken daily (dose/route not documented).
  - Oral rehydration solution (ORS, salt-sugar mix) — taken orally 3 times/day for past 2 days (dose not documented).
  - Ibuprofen occasionally for menstrual cramps (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Social history:
  - Occupation: Graphic designer; working from home today due to illness.
  - Lives with brother and mother.
  - Tobacco: Does not smoke.
  - Alcohol: Occasional (stated "a pint from time to time").
  - Recreational drugs: Denies.
  - Sexual history: Not currently sexually active; not using contraception; last menstrual period 2 weeks ago.
- Allergies: Not documented in the transcript.

Objective:
- No documented vital signs.
- No physical examination findings documented.
- No clinic-based investigations or laboratory results documented.
- Patient-reported findings: subjective fever by touch; reports passing urine ~1 hour prior to consult.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Infectious gastroenteritis:
   - Assessment/likely diagnosis: Infectious gastroenteritis.
   - Differential diagnosis:
     - Viral gastroenteritis.
     - Bacterial gastroenteritis.
   - Investigations planned:
     - Stool sample for microbiological testing (to rule out bacterial pathogens).
     - In-clinic assessment of hydration status.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Continue oral rehydration solution in very small, frequent sips to avoid provoking vomiting.
     - Advise simple, bland oral intake if tolerated (e.g., toast or biscuits); avoid fruit, raw vegetables, and milk while symptomatic.
     - Consider targeted antimicrobial therapy only if stool testing identifies a treatable bacterial pathogen (to be decided after results).
   - Relevant referrals:
     - Urgent clinic appointment to assess hydration and submit stool sample (to be arranged via support line).
     - Advise presentation to emergency department (A&E) if symptoms worsen or if unable to maintain hydration.

2. Dehydration (risk from ongoing vomiting and diarrhea):
   - Assessment/likely diagnosis: Dehydration (risk).
   - Differential diagnosis: N/A (risk related to ongoing fluid losses).
   - Investigations planned:
     - Clinical assessment of hydration in clinic (monitor urine output).
   - Treatment planned:
     - Continue small frequent oral rehydration as above.
     - If unable to tolerate oral fluids or clinical dehydration is confirmed, arrange emergency care for intravenous fluid resuscitation.
   - Relevant referrals:
     - Urgent clinic assessment now; A&E if deterioration or inability to maintain oral intake.

3. Periumbilical abdominal pain:
   - Assessment/likely diagnosis: Abdominal pain (periumbilical), likely secondary to gastroenteritis.
   - Differential diagnosis: N/A (clinical context suggests gastroenteritis; no additional differentials assessed in transcript).
   - Investigations planned:
     - No additional investigations documented beyond those for gastroenteritis.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Symptomatic management as part of gastroenteritis care; patient reports occasional use of ibuprofen for menstrual cramps (dose/route/frequency not documented).

Quality checks:
- Missing but expected elements:
  - Vital signs (temperature, pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate).
  - Physical examination findings (abdominal exam, hydration signs).
  - Pregnancy status or pregnancy test (patient not using contraception; last period 2 weeks ago — pregnancy not assessed).
  - Allergy status not documented.
  - Medication doses and routes largely incomplete (see medications section).
  - Stool sample results and any laboratory testing not yet available.
- Internal conflicts from the transcript:
  - None identified.
- Transcript quality comment:
  - Consultation audio/transcript contained occasional pauses and brief unintelligible segments, but overall clinically relevant information was retrievable.
